description: Curated, example-driven C# and .NET APIs for everyday application, automation, data, and systems work. No additional packages are required.
executionSupportMessage: Compatible with the built-in .NET 10 C# runner; authored against .NET 8.

actionDescriptions.Add: Adds a new value to an existing collection without replacing the collection itself.
actionDescriptions.Append: Writes new data after the content that is already present.
actionDescriptions.Calculate: Computes and returns a numerical result from the supplied values.
actionDescriptions.Clear: Removes existing content or entries while leaving the container available for reuse.
actionDescriptions.Combine: Builds one value from two or more separate values.
actionDescriptions.Convert: Changes a value into another representation or data type.
actionDescriptions.Copy: Creates another copy of existing data at a new destination.
actionDescriptions.Create: Constructs a new object or resource that did not exist before.
actionDescriptions.Deserialize: Reconstructs a typed in-memory object from stored or transmitted data.
actionDescriptions.Download: Requests data from a remote HTTP address and returns the received content.
actionDescriptions.Filter: Keeps only the values that satisfy a condition.
actionDescriptions.Find: Searches for a value or position and reports what was found.
actionDescriptions.Format: Produces a specific text representation or layout without changing the underlying value.
actionDescriptions.Get: Retrieves an existing value, resource, or collection without intentionally changing it.
actionDescriptions.Group: Organizes values into buckets that share the same key.
actionDescriptions.Join: Combines several values into one sequence or string.
actionDescriptions.Match: Applies a pattern and returns the matching text or match details.
actionDescriptions.Move: Relocates a resource from one path to another.
actionDescriptions.Order: Returns values arranged by a selected key.
actionDescriptions.Parse: Interprets text as a specific typed value and reports or throws when the text is invalid.
actionDescriptions.Read: Takes input from a user, stream, file, or response and returns it to the program.
actionDescriptions.Remove: Takes a value out of a collection or deletes a selected element.
actionDescriptions.Replace: Produces content in which selected values or matching text are substituted.
actionDescriptions.Select: Projects or extracts a particular part of a value or sequence.
actionDescriptions.Serialize: Turns an in-memory object into data that can be stored or transmitted.
actionDescriptions.Sort: Rearranges a mutable collection into ascending or custom order.
actionDescriptions.Split: Separates one value into multiple parts using a delimiter or pattern.
actionDescriptions.Start: Launches a process or initiates an operation.
actionDescriptions.Sum: Adds numeric values in a sequence and returns the total.
actionDescriptions.Test: Evaluates a condition and returns true or false without intentionally changing the target.
actionDescriptions.Wait: Asynchronously pauses until time passes or one or more operations finish.
actionDescriptions.Write: Sends text or data to an output destination.

objectDescriptions.Base64: Base64 is a text-safe encoding of binary bytes. It is useful for transport, but it is not encryption.
objectDescriptions.Console: The console is the application's standard text input and output interface, normally connected to a terminal window.
objectDescriptions.DateTime: DateTime is a value containing a calendar date and clock time, with optional local or UTC context.
objectDescriptions.Dictionary: Dictionary<TKey,TValue> stores unique keys paired with values and provides fast lookup by key.
objectDescriptions.Directory: A directory is a file-system container that can hold files and other directories.
objectDescriptions.Environment: Environment exposes information and settings associated with the current process and operating-system session.
objectDescriptions.File: A file is a named sequence of bytes stored by a file system; text helpers encode and decode those bytes as characters.
objectDescriptions.Guid: Guid is a 128-bit identifier designed to be unique across machines and time without a central counter.
objectDescriptions.HashSet: HashSet<T> stores unique values and supports mathematical set operations such as union and intersection.
objectDescriptions.HttpClient: HttpClient is a reusable client for sending HTTP requests and receiving HTTP responses.
objectDescriptions.HttpResponse: HttpResponseMessage represents an HTTP server's status code, headers, and response body.
objectDescriptions.Json: JSON is a text format for objects, arrays, strings, numbers, Boolean values, and null.
objectDescriptions.List: List<T> is an ordered, index-based collection whose size can grow or shrink.
objectDescriptions.Number: A number is a typed numeric value on which mathematical, comparison, and conversion operations can be performed.
objectDescriptions.Path: A path is text that identifies a file-system location; Path helpers manipulate the text without opening the resource.
objectDescriptions.Process: A process is a running instance of a program with its own identifier, memory, handles, and execution state.
objectDescriptions.Random: Random is a pseudo-random number generator for simulations and ordinary selection. It is not suitable for secrets or security tokens.
objectDescriptions.Regex: A regular expression is a pattern language for finding, validating, splitting, and replacing text.
objectDescriptions.Sequence: An IEnumerable<T> sequence is a stream of typed values. Many LINQ operations are lazy and run only when the sequence is enumerated.
objectDescriptions.String: A string is an immutable sequence of Unicode characters used to represent text.
objectDescriptions.Task: A Task represents work that may still be running and will eventually complete, fail, or be canceled.

commands.name: Console.WriteLine
commands.description: Write a value followed by a line break.
commands.definition: Writes the text representation of a value to standard output and then writes the current platform's line terminator. The next console output begins on a new line.

parameters.name: message
parameters.description: The value or string expression to display.

examples.title: Report a calculated result
examples.code:
var filesFound = 12;
Console.WriteLine($"Found {filesFound} files.");
examples.explanation: The interpolated expression inserts the current value of filesFound, writes the completed message, and moves the cursor to the next line.

commands.name: Console.Write
commands.description: Write a value without adding a line break.
commands.definition: Writes a value to standard output but leaves the cursor immediately after the text. This is useful for prompts or for building one line in several pieces.

parameters.name: message
parameters.description: The value or string expression to display.

examples.title: Prompt on the current line
examples.code:
Console.Write("Project name: ");
var projectName = Console.ReadLine();
examples.explanation: Because Write does not add a newline, the user's response appears on the same line as the prompt.

commands.name: Console.ReadLine
commands.description: Read one complete line of console input.
commands.definition: Waits for the user to enter text and press Enter, then returns the entered characters without the line terminator. It returns null when the input stream has ended.

examples.title: Read and validate a name
examples.explanation: ReadLine waits for Enter. The null-coalescing expression uses guest only if standard input has already closed.

commands.name: Console.ReadKey
commands.description: Read the next key pressed in the console.
commands.definition: Waits for a key press and returns a ConsoleKeyInfo containing the character and modifier keys. The intercept argument decides whether the pressed character is echoed to the terminal.

parameters.name: intercept
parameters.description: Use true to keep the pressed key from being displayed.

examples.title: Wait for confirmation without echoing
examples.explanation: ReadKey captures one key immediately. With intercept set to true, the original key is not printed before the result message.

commands.name: string.Contains
commands.description: Test whether text contains a specified value.
commands.definition: Returns true when the target string contains the supplied character sequence. An overload accepts StringComparison so the caller can choose ordinal or culture-aware, case-sensitive or case-insensitive matching.

examples.title: Perform a case-insensitive search
examples.explanation: OrdinalIgnoreCase makes REPORT match report without applying language-specific sorting rules.

commands.name: string.StartsWith
commands.description: Test whether text begins with a specified value.
commands.definition: Returns true when the beginning of the target string matches the supplied text. Supplying StringComparison makes the intended case and culture rules explicit.

examples.title: Recognize an HTTPS address
examples.explanation: Only the prefix is tested; the remainder of the address does not affect the result.

commands.name: string.EndsWith
commands.description: Test whether text ends with a specified value.
commands.definition: Returns true when the final characters of the target string match the supplied suffix. It is commonly used for extensions and naming conventions, but Path.GetExtension is safer for full file paths.

examples.title: Filter Markdown names
examples.explanation: The predicate keeps names ending in .md regardless of letter case.

commands.name: string.Replace
commands.description: Create text with matching content replaced.
commands.definition: Returns a new string in which every occurrence of the specified old text is replaced with new text. Strings are immutable, so the original string is unchanged.

examples.title: Normalize a path separator
examples.explanation: Every backslash character is replaced in the returned string; portablePath keeps its original value.

commands.name: string.Split
commands.description: Separate text into an array of substrings.
commands.definition: Breaks a string wherever a delimiter occurs and returns the resulting pieces. Options can remove empty entries and trim whitespace during the split.

examples.title: Parse a comma-separated list
examples.explanation: The options trim each piece and discard the empty field, producing alpha, beta, and gamma.

commands.name: string.Join
commands.description: Combine values into one delimited string.
commands.definition: Concatenates the text representation of each supplied value and inserts the separator between adjacent values. It does not place the separator before the first or after the last value.

parameters.name: values
parameters.description: The sequence or array to combine.

examples.title: Build a readable label list
examples.explanation: The three labels become one string: bug, urgent, backend.

commands.name: string.Trim
commands.description: Remove leading and trailing whitespace.
commands.definition: Returns a new string with whitespace removed from both ends. Characters inside the string are preserved, and an overload can trim a caller-supplied set of characters instead.

examples.title: Clean console input
examples.explanation: The spaces at both edges disappear; the hyphen and internal characters remain.

commands.name: string.ToUpperInvariant
commands.description: Create an uppercase string using culture-independent rules.
commands.definition: Returns an uppercase copy using the invariant culture. This is useful for machine-oriented identifiers; user-facing text often needs a specific CultureInfo instead.

examples.title: Normalize a command token
examples.explanation: Normalization lets the switch compare one predictable representation of the token.

commands.name: string.ToLowerInvariant
commands.description: Create a lowercase string using culture-independent rules.
commands.definition: Returns a lowercase copy using invariant-culture casing rules. It is appropriate for normalized protocol or identifier text, not for every language-sensitive display task.

examples.title: Normalize a file extension
examples.explanation: The uppercase extension is converted to .pdf before comparison.

commands.name: string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace
commands.description: Test whether text is missing or contains only whitespace.
commands.definition: Returns true for null, the empty string, or a string made entirely of whitespace characters. It is a concise guard for required text input.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: The nullable string expression to validate.

examples.title: Reject an empty project name
examples.explanation: The guard catches end-of-input, an empty response, and a response containing only spaces or tabs.

commands.name: string.IndexOf
commands.description: Find the zero-based position of text.
commands.definition: Searches the target string and returns the index where the requested character sequence first begins. It returns -1 when no match exists.

examples.title: Locate a separator
examples.explanation: IndexOf finds the equals sign, and range expressions use that position to split the key from its value.

commands.name: string.Substring
commands.description: Extract part of a string by position.
commands.definition: Returns a new string beginning at a zero-based index and optionally limited to a specified length. Invalid indexes or lengths throw ArgumentOutOfRangeException.

parameters.name: startIndex
parameters.description: The zero-based first character to include.

parameters.name: length
parameters.description: The number of characters to return.

examples.title: Read a date prefix
examples.explanation: Starting at index 0 and taking 10 characters returns 2026-07-27.

commands.name: File.ReadAllText
commands.description: Read an entire text file into one string.
commands.definition: Opens a text file, decodes all of its content, returns it as one string, and closes the file. Use a streaming API when the file may be too large to hold comfortably in memory.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: The path of the text file to read.

examples.title: Read and display a configuration file
examples.explanation: Path.Combine builds the location, ReadAllText loads the complete file, and Console.WriteLine displays the returned string.

commands.name: File.ReadAllTextAsync
commands.description: Asynchronously read an entire text file.
commands.definition: Reads all text without blocking the calling thread while operating-system I/O is pending. Await returns the complete string, and a CancellationToken overload can cancel the operation.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: The path of the text file to read.

examples.title: Load text without blocking
examples.explanation: await yields control while the file read is pending, then resumes with the complete text.

commands.name: File.ReadAllLines
commands.description: Read a text file into an array of lines.
commands.definition: Reads every line from a text file, closes the file, and returns a string array with one element per line. Line terminator characters are not included in the returned strings.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: The path of the text file to read.

examples.title: Process a file line by line
examples.explanation: Each file line becomes a separate array element that the loop can process independently.

commands.name: File.WriteAllText
commands.description: Create or replace a text file.
commands.definition: Writes the complete string to a file, creating the file if necessary and replacing its prior contents if it already exists. The method closes the file before returning.

examples.title: Save application state
examples.explanation: The directory is ensured first, then WriteAllText creates or fully replaces state.json.

commands.name: File.WriteAllTextAsync
commands.description: Asynchronously create or replace a text file.
commands.definition: Writes a complete string while allowing the caller to remain responsive during pending I/O. Await completes only after the content has been written and the file has been closed.

examples.title: Save a report asynchronously
examples.explanation: The success message is reached after the asynchronous write has finished.

commands.name: File.AppendAllText
commands.description: Append text to the end of a file.
commands.definition: Opens or creates a text file, writes the supplied content after any existing content, and closes it. Add your own newline when each append should begin on a new line.

examples.title: Append a timestamped log entry
examples.code:
var entry = $"{DateTimeOffset.Now:O} Application started{Environment.NewLine}";
File.AppendAllText("activity.log", entry);
examples.explanation: The ISO timestamp and newline are added after earlier log entries; the prior file content is preserved.

commands.name: File.Exists
commands.description: Test whether a file path currently exists.
commands.definition: Returns true when the path identifies an existing file. It returns false for missing paths, directories, invalid paths, and many access-related failures rather than throwing those failures.

examples.title: Load an optional settings file
examples.explanation: The file is read only when it exists; otherwise the program uses an empty JSON object.

commands.name: File.Copy
commands.description: Copy a file to another path.
commands.definition: Creates a second file containing the source file's data. The overwrite argument controls whether an existing destination file may be replaced.

parameters.name: overwrite
parameters.description: Whether an existing destination may be replaced.

examples.title: Create a replaceable backup
examples.explanation: The source remains in place, while the backup path receives a fresh copy even if an older backup exists.

commands.name: File.Move
commands.description: Move or rename a file.
commands.definition: Relocates a file to another path, which can also change its name. On the same volume this is usually a metadata operation; overloads can optionally replace an existing destination.

parameters.name: overwrite
parameters.description: Whether an existing destination may be replaced.

examples.title: Archive a completed download
examples.explanation: The temporary file is relocated and renamed package.zip inside the archive directory.

commands.name: File.Delete
commands.description: Delete a file.
commands.definition: Permanently removes the file at the supplied path. Calling it for a missing file does nothing, but invalid paths, access failures, and in-use files can throw exceptions.

examples.title: Remove an expired temporary file
examples.explanation: The existence check makes the intent explicit; Delete then removes the file rather than sending it to a recycle bin.

commands.name: Directory.CreateDirectory
commands.description: Create a directory and any missing parents.
commands.definition: Ensures that the specified directory path exists, creating every missing directory in the path. It succeeds without replacing content when the directory already exists.

examples.title: Prepare a nested output folder
examples.explanation: CreateDirectory makes build, reports, and daily as needed before the file is written.

commands.name: Directory.GetFiles
commands.description: Return file paths from a directory.
commands.definition: Immediately enumerates matching files and returns their paths as a string array. A search pattern limits names, and an overload can include subdirectories.

examples.title: List log files
examples.explanation: GetFiles returns the matching paths as an array, and the loop prints just each file name.

commands.name: Directory.EnumerateFiles
commands.description: Lazily enumerate file paths from a directory.
commands.definition: Returns an IEnumerable<string> that produces matching file paths as they are requested. Unlike GetFiles, processing can begin before every match has been collected in memory.

examples.title: Stop after the first ten source files
examples.explanation: Lazy enumeration lets Take stop the directory walk after ten matching paths have been requested.

commands.name: Directory.GetDirectories
commands.description: Return child directory paths.
commands.definition: Returns a string array containing directories that match the selected path and optional search pattern. SearchOption can limit the operation to direct children or recurse through the tree.

examples.title: Show immediate project folders
examples.explanation: Only the direct child directories are returned by this overload.

commands.name: Directory.Exists
commands.description: Test whether a directory path currently exists.
commands.definition: Returns true when the path identifies an existing directory. Missing, invalid, and inaccessible paths normally produce false rather than an exception.

examples.title: Choose an available workspace
examples.explanation: The preferred directory is used when available; otherwise the current process directory becomes the fallback.

commands.name: Directory.Delete
commands.description: Delete a directory.
commands.definition: Removes a directory. The recursive argument must be true to delete a non-empty tree, so callers should resolve and validate the exact target before using it.

examples.title: Remove a known build-output folder
examples.explanation: The code resolves one explicit target, checks it, and removes the tree. Recursive deletion is permanent and should never use an unvalidated broad path.

commands.name: Path.Combine
commands.description: Combine path segments with the proper separator.
commands.definition: Joins path segments using the current platform's directory separator rules. If a later segment is rooted, earlier segments may be discarded, so untrusted rooted input should be validated.

examples.title: Build a settings path
examples.explanation: Each segment is joined with the separator appropriate for the operating system.

commands.name: Path.GetFileName
commands.description: Extract the file-name portion of a path.
commands.definition: Returns the characters after the final directory separator. The result can include an extension and is empty when the path ends in a separator.

examples.title: Display only a file name
examples.code:
var fullPath = @"C:\logs\app-2026.log";
Console.WriteLine(Path.GetFileName(fullPath));
examples.explanation: The directory portion is removed and app-2026.log is returned.

commands.name: Path.GetExtension
commands.description: Extract the extension from a path.
commands.definition: Returns the final period and the characters that follow it in the last path segment. It returns an empty string when no extension is present.

examples.title: Route files by extension
examples.explanation: GetExtension returns only the final extension, .gz, not the earlier .tar portion.

commands.name: Path.GetDirectoryName
commands.description: Extract the directory portion of a path.
commands.definition: Returns the path text before the final directory separator, or null when the input has no directory information. It manipulates path text and does not check whether the directory exists.

examples.title: Ensure a destination parent exists
examples.explanation: The parent path is extracted from the full destination and created before a later file write.

commands.name: Path.GetFullPath
commands.description: Resolve a path to an absolute normalized path.
commands.definition: Converts relative path text into a fully qualified path using a base directory and normalizes components such as dot segments. It does not require the resulting file or directory to exist.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: The relative or absolute path to resolve.

examples.title: Resolve a user-supplied relative path
examples.explanation: The result is absolute and the data\.. pair is normalized away.

commands.name: Path.ChangeExtension
commands.description: Return a path with a different extension.
commands.definition: Produces new path text whose final extension is replaced, added, or removed. It does not rename or create a file on disk.

parameters.name: extension
parameters.description: The new extension, with or without a leading period.

examples.title: Build a sidecar metadata name
examples.explanation: The returned text is photos\sunset.json; the original JPG file is untouched.

commands.name: Path.GetTempPath
commands.description: Get the current user's temporary-file directory.
commands.definition: Returns the path the operating system designates for temporary files for the current process or user. The method returns a directory path but does not create a unique file within it.

examples.title: Build a unique temporary file path
examples.explanation: GetTempPath chooses the temporary directory and GetRandomFileName supplies a low-collision name inside it.

commands.name: Path.GetRandomFileName
commands.description: Generate a random file name without creating a file.
commands.definition: Returns a cryptographically strong random name suitable for use as a file or directory name. It does not create anything, so the caller still chooses a directory and handles the small possibility of a collision.

examples.title: Create an isolated temporary directory
examples.explanation: The random name becomes one child of the operating system's temporary directory, then CreateDirectory makes it real.

commands.name: List<T>.Add
commands.description: Add one item to the end of a list.
commands.definition: Appends one value to a mutable List<T>, increasing Count by one. The value must be compatible with the list's element type.

examples.title: Collect validation errors
examples.explanation: The message is appended only when validation fails, and the list can later display all collected errors.

commands.name: List<T>.AddRange
commands.description: Append every item from another sequence.
commands.definition: Enumerates the supplied collection and appends each value to the list in order. The existing list entries remain before the newly added range.

parameters.name: items
parameters.description: The sequence of values to append.

examples.title: Merge discovered files into a work list
examples.explanation: README.md stays first, followed by every source-file path produced by the enumeration.

commands.name: List<T>.Remove
commands.description: Remove the first matching value from a list.
commands.definition: Searches from the beginning of the list, removes the first equal item, and returns true. It returns false and leaves the list unchanged when no equal item exists.

examples.title: Remove a completed task
examples.explanation: Remove returns true because Test was found, and the remaining list contains Build and Deploy.

commands.name: List<T>.RemoveAt
commands.description: Remove the item at a zero-based index.
commands.definition: Deletes exactly one element by position and shifts all later elements down by one index. An index outside the current list range throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException.

examples.title: Remove the oldest queue entry
examples.explanation: After the count guard, index 0 is safe to remove and middle becomes the first entry.

commands.name: List<T>.Contains
commands.description: Test whether a list contains an equal value.
commands.definition: Searches the list using its element equality comparer and returns true when an equal value is present. For strings, the default comparison is case-sensitive.

examples.title: Avoid adding a duplicate ID
examples.explanation: Contains finds 203, so the guarded Add does not create a duplicate.

commands.name: List<T>.Find
commands.description: Find the first list item that satisfies a predicate.
commands.definition: Runs a Boolean predicate against list elements in order and returns the first match. When nothing matches it returns default(T), which can be ambiguous for value types.

parameters.name: predicate
parameters.description: A function returning true for the desired item.

examples.title: Find a user by ID
examples.explanation: The predicate selects the first User whose Id is 12, so Grace is printed.

commands.name: List<T>.Sort
commands.description: Sort a list in place.
commands.definition: Reorders the existing List<T> rather than returning a second sequence. With no comparer it uses the element type's default ordering; overloads accept comparison logic.

examples.title: Sort version labels with a comparison
examples.explanation: The list itself becomes 1.2, 1.5, 2.0 using Version's default comparison.

commands.name: Dictionary<TKey,TValue>.Add
commands.description: Add a new key and value to a dictionary.
commands.definition: Stores a key-value pair and requires the key to be absent. Adding an equal key twice throws ArgumentException; use TryAdd or assignment when duplicate keys are expected.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The value associated with the key.

examples.title: Register a command handler
examples.explanation: The comparer makes key lookup case-insensitive, and the stored Action is invoked by its build key.

commands.name: Dictionary<TKey,TValue>.TryGetValue
commands.description: Look up a value without throwing when the key is absent.
commands.definition: Attempts one dictionary lookup, places the found value in an out variable, and returns true on success. On failure it returns false and assigns default(TValue).

examples.title: Read an optional timeout
examples.explanation: The existing value 30 is returned; if the key were missing, the conditional would use 10.

commands.name: Dictionary<TKey,TValue>.ContainsKey
commands.description: Test whether a dictionary contains a key.
commands.definition: Returns true when the dictionary contains an equal key according to its key comparer. When the value is also needed, TryGetValue avoids performing a second lookup.

examples.title: Add a default only when missing
examples.explanation: The assignment runs only when no https key exists.

commands.name: Dictionary<TKey,TValue>.Remove
commands.description: Remove an entry by key.
commands.definition: Deletes the key and its associated value, returning true when an entry was present. An overload also returns the removed value through an out parameter.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: The key of the entry to remove.

examples.title: Remove and inspect a cached value
examples.explanation: The entry disappears from the dictionary while its former value remains available in removedValue.

commands.name: Dictionary<TKey,TValue>.Clear
commands.description: Remove every entry from a dictionary.
commands.definition: Deletes all key-value pairs and sets Count to zero while retaining the same dictionary instance, comparer, and reusable allocated storage.

examples.title: Reset an in-memory cache
examples.explanation: The same cache object remains usable, but it contains zero entries.

commands.name: HashSet<T>.Add
commands.description: Add a value only if it is not already in the set.
commands.definition: Inserts a unique value and returns true. When an equal value is already present, it returns false and the set remains unchanged.

examples.title: Collect unique file extensions
examples.explanation: Repeated extensions are ignored, and the comparer treats .TXT and .txt as the same value.

commands.name: HashSet<T>.Contains
commands.description: Test whether a set contains an equal value.
commands.definition: Uses the set's equality comparer to perform a fast membership test. It returns a Boolean and does not change the set.

examples.title: Authorize a role
examples.explanation: The case-insensitive set recognizes operator as the existing Operator role.

commands.name: HashSet<T>.UnionWith
commands.description: Add every distinct value from another sequence.
commands.definition: Mutates the set so it contains values that appeared in either the original set or the supplied sequence. Duplicates remain collapsed according to the set's comparer.

parameters.name: other
parameters.description: The values to merge into the set.

examples.title: Merge permission sets
examples.explanation: The result contains read, write, and deploy; the repeated write value appears only once.

commands.name: HashSet<T>.IntersectWith
commands.description: Keep only values that also occur in another sequence.
commands.definition: Mutates the set to its mathematical intersection with the supplied values. Every value not present in both collections is removed.

examples.title: Restrict requested features to supported features
examples.explanation: tracing is removed because it is not supported; logs and metrics remain.

commands.name: Enumerable.Where
commands.description: Keep sequence elements that satisfy a condition.
commands.definition: Returns a lazy sequence that yields only source elements for which the predicate returns true. The source is evaluated when the result is enumerated, not when Where is called.

parameters.name: predicate
parameters.description: A function that returns true for values to keep.

examples.title: Keep only large files
examples.explanation: Each path is tested during enumeration, and only files larger than one million bytes reach the loop.

commands.name: Enumerable.Select
commands.description: Transform every sequence element into a result value.
commands.definition: Returns a lazy projection in which the selector function converts each source element to another value or shape. It does not mutate the source objects unless the selector itself does so.

parameters.name: selector
parameters.description: A function that creates one result per source value.

examples.title: Project file paths into names
examples.explanation: Each full path is replaced in the result sequence by its file-name portion.

commands.name: Enumerable.OrderBy
commands.description: Order sequence elements by an ascending key.
commands.definition: Returns a new ordered sequence using the key produced for each element. The source collection is not rearranged, and enumeration performs the ordering work.

parameters.name: keySelector
parameters.description: A function that returns the sort key.

examples.title: Order processes by memory use
examples.explanation: The five processes with the smallest working sets are enumerated first.

commands.name: Enumerable.OrderByDescending
commands.description: Order sequence elements by a descending key.
commands.definition: Returns an ordered sequence with larger or later key values first. The operation leaves the original collection unchanged.

parameters.name: keySelector
parameters.description: A function that returns the sort key.

examples.title: Show the newest files first
examples.explanation: FileInfo objects are sorted by UTC modification time, newest first, and only the first three are kept.

commands.name: Enumerable.GroupBy
commands.description: Group sequence elements that share a key.
commands.definition: Returns groups keyed by the value produced for each source element. Every group is itself an enumerable sequence, and all elements with equal keys appear together.

parameters.name: keySelector
parameters.description: A function that chooses each grouping key.

examples.title: Count files by extension
examples.explanation: Paths sharing an extension are collected into the same group, then each group's size is printed.

commands.name: Enumerable.Any
commands.description: Test whether a sequence has any matching element.
commands.definition: Returns true as soon as one element satisfies the predicate, so it need not enumerate the rest. Without a predicate it tests whether the sequence contains at least one element.

parameters.name: predicate
parameters.description: The condition at least one element must satisfy.

examples.title: Check for failed results
examples.explanation: Enumeration stops when exit code 2 satisfies the predicate, and true is returned.

commands.name: Enumerable.All
commands.description: Test whether every sequence element satisfies a condition.
commands.definition: Returns false as soon as one element fails the predicate. It returns true for an empty sequence because no element violates the condition.

parameters.name: predicate
parameters.description: The condition every element must satisfy.

examples.title: Validate all configured ports
examples.explanation: Every port lies inside the legal numeric range, so All returns true.

commands.name: Enumerable.FirstOrDefault
commands.description: Return the first matching element or a default value.
commands.definition: Returns the first source element, or the first one satisfying a predicate. When no element exists it returns default(T), commonly null for reference types and zero for int.

examples.title: Find the first JSON file
examples.explanation: Enumeration stops at the first matching path; null produces the fallback message.

commands.name: Enumerable.SingleOrDefault
commands.description: Return the only matching element, or a default when none exists.
commands.definition: Returns one element when exactly one match exists and default(T) when none exists. It throws InvalidOperationException if more than one element matches, making duplicate data visible.

examples.title: Require a unique user ID
examples.explanation: No match yields null; duplicate IDs throw instead of silently choosing one record.

commands.name: Enumerable.Distinct
commands.description: Return one occurrence of each distinct value.
commands.definition: Produces a lazy sequence that omits later values considered equal by the selected comparer. It preserves the first-seen order in the current implementation, but callers should not depend on undocumented ordering guarantees.

examples.title: Remove duplicate tags
examples.explanation: The case-insensitive comparer treats CSharp and csharp as duplicates.

commands.name: Enumerable.Count
commands.description: Count elements in a sequence.
commands.definition: Returns the number of source elements, or the number satisfying a predicate. It can use a collection's Count directly, but otherwise enumerates the sequence to calculate the result.

parameters.name: predicate
parameters.description: The optional condition for values to count.

examples.title: Count enabled features
examples.explanation: Only Search and Preview satisfy the predicate, so the result is 2.

commands.name: Enumerable.Sum
commands.description: Add numeric sequence values.
commands.definition: Enumerates numeric values and returns their total. Selector overloads first extract a numeric value from each object, and overflow behavior depends on the numeric type.

parameters.name: selector
parameters.description: The optional function that supplies each number.

examples.title: Total file sizes
examples.explanation: The selector reads each FileInfo.Length and Sum adds those long integer values.

commands.name: Enumerable.Take
commands.description: Return at most the first requested number of elements.
commands.definition: Produces a lazy sequence containing the first count elements, or every element when the source is shorter. It stops requesting source values after the limit is reached.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: The maximum number of values to return.

examples.title: Display the five newest reports
examples.explanation: Ordering places newest paths first and Take limits the displayed result to five.

commands.name: Enumerable.Skip
commands.description: Ignore a requested number of leading elements.
commands.definition: Returns a lazy sequence that discards the first count values and yields the remainder. If the source has fewer elements, the result is empty.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: The number of leading values to ignore.

examples.title: Select the second page of results
examples.explanation: Skip ignores the first page's 20 values and Take returns at most 20 values for page two.

commands.name: Enumerable.ToList
commands.description: Materialize a sequence into a new list.
commands.definition: Enumerates the source immediately and copies its current values into a new List<T>. Later source changes do not automatically update that list.

examples.title: Capture the current matching files
examples.explanation: ToList performs the directory enumeration now and stores the paths in a mutable list.

commands.name: JsonSerializer.Serialize
commands.description: Serialize a .NET value into JSON text.
commands.definition: Inspects the value's public data and produces a JSON string according to its .NET type and JsonSerializerOptions. The output is data, not executable C# source.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: Formatting, naming, converter, and reference-handling settings.

examples.title: Write an indented settings document
examples.explanation: The record becomes indented JSON text, which is then saved as a file.

commands.name: JsonSerializer.Deserialize<T>
commands.description: Deserialize JSON text into a typed .NET value.
commands.definition: Parses JSON and creates an instance of T by mapping JSON properties to the type's serializable members. Invalid JSON can throw JsonException, and a literal JSON null can produce null.

examples.title: Load typed application settings
examples.explanation: The JSON text is parsed into a typed dictionary, and the null guard rejects a JSON null document.

commands.name: JsonSerializer.SerializeAsync
commands.description: Asynchronously write a .NET value as JSON to a stream.
commands.definition: Serializes a value directly into a Stream without first requiring one complete JSON string in memory. Await completes after the JSON bytes have been written.

examples.title: Stream a report into a file
examples.explanation: File.Create supplies the writable stream, and await using ensures it is disposed after serialization finishes.

commands.name: JsonSerializer.DeserializeAsync<T>
commands.description: Asynchronously read a typed value from a JSON stream.
commands.definition: Reads UTF-8 JSON from a Stream and reconstructs an instance of T while allowing the caller to remain responsive during pending I/O. Malformed or incompatible content can throw JsonException.

examples.title: Read JSON from a stream
examples.explanation: The UTF-8 JSON is consumed from a stream and converted directly into a typed dictionary.

commands.name: HttpClient.GetStringAsync
commands.description: Download an HTTP response body as text.
commands.definition: Sends an HTTP GET request and asynchronously returns the response content as a string. It throws for an unsuccessful status code and should normally use a reused HttpClient instance.

examples.title: Download and parse JSON
examples.explanation: GetStringAsync returns the response body, and JsonDocument reads the selected property without requiring an application-specific model type.

commands.name: HttpClient.GetAsync
commands.description: Send an HTTP GET request and keep the full response.
commands.definition: Asynchronously returns an HttpResponseMessage containing status, headers, and content. Unlike GetStringAsync, it lets the caller inspect non-success responses before deciding how to handle them.

examples.title: Inspect status before reading content
examples.explanation: The response object exposes status metadata and owns the content stream, so it is disposed after the body is read.

commands.name: HttpClient.PostAsJsonAsync
commands.description: Serialize a value as JSON and send it with HTTP POST.
commands.definition: Uses System.Net.Http.Json extensions to serialize a .NET value into a JSON request body, sets an application/json content type, and asynchronously returns the full response.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The object to send as JSON.

examples.title: Create an API record
examples.explanation: The request record is serialized into the POST body, and the final call turns a non-success response into an exception.

commands.name: HttpClient.SendAsync
commands.description: Send a fully customized HTTP request.
commands.definition: Asynchronously sends an HttpRequestMessage whose method, URI, headers, version, and content the caller controls. It returns the response without automatically requiring a successful status.

examples.title: Send an authenticated PATCH request
examples.explanation: HttpRequestMessage provides control over PATCH, the authorization header, and the JSON body before SendAsync transmits it.

commands.name: HttpResponseMessage.EnsureSuccessStatusCode
commands.description: Require an HTTP success status.
commands.definition: Returns the same response when its status code is in the 200–299 range. Otherwise it throws HttpRequestException, preventing later code from silently treating an error response as successful data.

examples.title: Fail before parsing an error page
examples.explanation: Only a 2xx response reaches body processing; an error status throws with HTTP context.

commands.name: DateTime.Now
commands.description: Get the current local date and time.
commands.definition: Returns a DateTime representing the computer's current local clock with Kind set to Local. Use UtcNow for storage, distributed systems, and comparisons that should not depend on a local time zone.

examples.title: Display a local timestamp
examples.code:
var now = DateTime.Now;
Console.WriteLine(now.ToString("yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss"));
examples.explanation: Now reads the local system clock and ToString formats it for display.

commands.name: DateTime.UtcNow
commands.description: Get the current Coordinated Universal Time.
commands.definition: Returns the current clock time in UTC with Kind set to Utc. UTC timestamps avoid ambiguity between computers in different time zones, though DateTimeOffset is often better when an offset must be preserved.

examples.title: Create an unambiguous log timestamp
examples.code:
var line = $"{DateTime.UtcNow:O} deployment started";
File.AppendAllText("deploy.log", line + Environment.NewLine);
examples.explanation: The round-trip O format includes full precision and a UTC designator suitable for logs.

commands.name: DateTime.Parse
commands.description: Parse date-and-time text or throw when invalid.
commands.definition: Interprets text using a culture and style rules and returns a DateTime. It throws FormatException for invalid text, so TryParse is preferable for ordinary user input.

examples.title: Parse a controlled ISO date
examples.explanation: A known machine-generated format is parsed with explicit invariant-culture rules.

commands.name: DateTime.TryParse
commands.description: Try to parse date-and-time text without throwing for bad input.
commands.definition: Returns true and assigns the parsed DateTime when the text is valid under the selected culture and styles. Invalid text returns false and assigns the default DateTime value.
commands.template: var valid = DateTime.TryParse({text}, out var date);

examples.title: Validate a user-entered deadline
examples.explanation: Bad input follows the else branch instead of producing a FormatException.

commands.name: DateTime.AddDays
commands.description: Create a DateTime shifted by a number of days.
commands.definition: Returns a new DateTime offset by the supplied whole or fractional day count. DateTime is immutable, so the original value remains unchanged.

parameters.name: days
parameters.description: Positive or negative days to add.

examples.title: Calculate a seven-day expiration
examples.explanation: expiresUtc is seven days later, while createdUtc still holds the original timestamp.

commands.name: Regex.IsMatch
commands.description: Test whether text contains a regular-expression match.
commands.definition: Returns true when the regex engine finds at least one match for the pattern. Invalid patterns throw ArgumentException, and timeouts should be considered for patterns applied to untrusted input.

examples.title: Validate a simple identifier
examples.explanation: The anchors require the entire string to match, the first character must be a letter, and later characters may include digits, underscore, or hyphen.

commands.name: Regex.Match
commands.description: Find the first regex match and capture its groups.
commands.definition: Searches input and returns a Match object describing the first occurrence, including its text, position, length, and named or numbered capture groups. Match.Success indicates whether anything matched.

examples.title: Extract a key and numeric value
examples.explanation: Named groups capture timeout separately from 30 after the complete input matches.

commands.name: Regex.Replace
commands.description: Replace every substring matching a pattern.
commands.definition: Returns new text in which regex matches are replaced by fixed text or by values computed in a MatchEvaluator. The original input string is unchanged.

examples.title: Collapse repeated whitespace
examples.explanation: Every run of one or more whitespace characters becomes exactly one space.

commands.name: Regex.Split
commands.description: Split text wherever a regex pattern matches.
commands.definition: Returns an array of text segments separated by pattern matches. Capturing groups in the pattern can also appear in the returned array, which differs from a simple string delimiter split.

examples.title: Split on commas or semicolons
examples.explanation: The pattern accepts either delimiter and consumes optional surrounding whitespace, producing alpha|beta|gamma.

commands.name: Task.Delay
commands.description: Asynchronously wait for a duration.
commands.definition: Returns a Task that completes after the requested interval without blocking a thread during the wait. A CancellationToken overload can end the delay early.

examples.title: Retry after a short backoff
examples.explanation: Each failed attempt awaits a progressively longer delay without tying up a worker thread.

commands.name: Task.WhenAll
commands.description: Wait asynchronously for every supplied task.
commands.definition: Returns one task that completes when all input tasks finish. Await produces all results for generic tasks and propagates failures after the group has completed.

examples.title: Download several pages concurrently
examples.explanation: All GET requests are started before WhenAll is awaited, allowing their I/O waits to overlap.

commands.name: Task.WhenAny
commands.description: Wait asynchronously until one supplied task finishes.
commands.definition: Returns a task whose result is the first input Task to reach a terminal state. Await the returned inner task again to obtain its value or observe its exception.

examples.title: Apply an operation timeout
examples.explanation: WhenAny identifies which task completed first; the operation is awaited again to retrieve its result and propagate failures.

commands.name: Task.Run
commands.description: Schedule CPU-bound work on the thread pool.
commands.definition: Queues a delegate to run on a thread-pool thread and returns a Task representing that work. It can keep a UI responsive during CPU-bound work, but it does not make synchronous I/O truly asynchronous.

examples.title: Calculate a hash away from the UI thread
examples.explanation: The hashing work runs on a thread-pool thread, and the awaiting UI code resumes with the result.

commands.name: Process.Start
commands.description: Start a process or open a shell-associated resource.
commands.definition: Creates a new operating-system process from a ProcessStartInfo and returns a Process object when one is available. UseShellExecute controls whether the OS shell may open documents and URLs instead of directly launching an executable.

parameters.name: startInfo
parameters.description: The executable, arguments, shell behavior, and startup settings.

examples.title: Run an executable with a safe argument list
examples.explanation: ArgumentList avoids hand-built command-line quoting, and the code asynchronously waits for the launched process to exit.

commands.name: Process.GetProcesses
commands.description: Get processes running on the local computer.
commands.definition: Returns Process components representing the processes visible to the caller at that moment. Process state can change immediately, and each returned component should be disposed after use.

examples.title: Display the five largest working sets
examples.explanation: The snapshot is ordered by memory use, and finally disposes every Process wrapper even if reading one property fails.

commands.name: Process.GetCurrentProcess
commands.description: Get a Process component for the running application.
commands.definition: Returns a Process object representing the caller's own operating-system process. It exposes the process ID, memory metrics, start time, threads, and other available runtime information.

examples.title: Report this application's process ID
examples.explanation: The Process wrapper reads information about the application that is executing this code, then is disposed.

commands.name: Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable
commands.description: Read an environment-variable value.
commands.definition: Looks up a named variable in the current process environment and returns its string value. It returns null when the name is not defined; target overloads can inspect user or machine variables on supported systems.

examples.title: Read an optional API endpoint
examples.explanation: A missing or invalid variable falls back to a known absolute URI.

commands.name: Environment.SetEnvironmentVariable
commands.description: Set or remove an environment-variable value.
commands.definition: Changes an environment variable for the current process by default; user and machine targets are also available where supported and permitted. Passing null removes the variable from the selected target.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The new value, or null to remove it.

examples.title: Configure a child process through its own environment
examples.explanation: For child-process configuration, editing ProcessStartInfo.Environment scopes the value to that child instead of changing the whole current process.

commands.name: Guid.NewGuid
commands.description: Create a new random GUID.
commands.definition: Returns a new 128-bit identifier with an extremely low collision probability. It is useful for identifiers, not as proof of identity or as a secret.

examples.title: Assign an ID to a new record
examples.explanation: The record receives a new identifier independently of its name and creation time.

commands.name: Guid.TryParse
commands.description: Try to parse GUID text without throwing for bad input.
commands.definition: Returns true and assigns the parsed Guid when the text has a recognized GUID format. Invalid or missing text returns false and assigns Guid.Empty.
commands.template: var valid = Guid.TryParse({text}, out var id);

examples.title: Validate an ID from a route
examples.explanation: Invalid route text takes the error branch; only a successfully parsed Guid is displayed as a validated ID.

commands.name: Convert.ToInt32
commands.description: Convert a compatible value to a 32-bit integer.
commands.definition: Converts supported primitive or string values into Int32 using defined rounding and culture behavior. Invalid text, overflow, or unsupported values can throw; int.TryParse is safer for untrusted text.

examples.title: Convert a Boolean setting to a numeric flag
examples.explanation: Convert maps true to 1 and false to 0. User-entered numeric text should normally use int.TryParse instead.

commands.name: Convert.ToBase64String
commands.description: Encode bytes as Base64 text.
commands.definition: Converts binary bytes into a Base64 string made from a restricted text alphabet. The encoding is reversible and transport-friendly but provides no secrecy.

examples.title: Embed a small binary value in JSON
examples.explanation: The image bytes become ordinary text that JSON can carry; a receiver must decode them to recover the image.

commands.name: Convert.FromBase64String
commands.description: Decode Base64 text into bytes.
commands.definition: Reconstructs the original byte array from valid Base64 text, ignoring permitted whitespace. Invalid alphabet, padding, or length produces FormatException.

examples.title: Restore an encoded attachment
examples.explanation: Valid text is decoded and written as bytes; malformed input is handled explicitly.

commands.name: Math.Round
commands.description: Round a floating-point or decimal value.
commands.definition: Returns the nearest value at the requested number of fractional digits. The overload's MidpointRounding choice determines how exact halfway values are handled.

parameters.name: digits
parameters.description: The number of fractional digits to retain.

examples.title: Round currency with an explicit midpoint rule
examples.explanation: The explicit rule turns the midpoint into 10.13 instead of relying on the default banker's rounding behavior.

commands.name: Math.Clamp
commands.description: Restrict a comparable value to a minimum and maximum.
commands.definition: Returns the minimum when the value is too small, the maximum when it is too large, and the value itself when it is inside the range. It throws when the maximum is less than the minimum.

examples.title: Constrain an opacity percentage
examples.explanation: The out-of-range request becomes 100, then converts to an opacity value of 1.0.

commands.name: Random.Next
commands.description: Generate a pseudo-random integer in a range.
commands.definition: Returns an integer greater than or equal to the minimum and strictly less than the maximum. Random.Shared is convenient and thread-safe for ordinary use; security-sensitive values require RandomNumberGenerator.

examples.title: Choose a random list item
examples.explanation: The exclusive upper bound guarantees the returned index is valid for the array.
